cards.explanation: The answer is that the fire must be kept burning. The burnt offering stays on the altar's hearth all night, and the fire has to keep burning the whole time. Leviticus 6:13 comes back to it: "The fire shall be kept burning on the altar continually; it must not be extinguished." Every morning the priest adds wood to that fire (Leviticus 6:12). So the fire stays lit, night and morning.

The answer is as a pleasing aroma to the LORD. The priest burns the memorial portion on the altar "…as a pleasing aroma to the LORD" (Leviticus 6:15). That handful is fine flour and olive oil, with all the frankincense. The text names the aroma as the purpose, friends, and it doesn't add any other.

The word is "eat." After the handful goes up on the altar, the rest is for Aaron and his sons to eat. The text says it's eaten without leaven, in a holy place, in the courtyard of the Tent of Meeting (Leviticus 6:16). Leviticus 6:17 calls it their portion of God's food offerings, so the leftovers go to the priests by God's own assignment.

The answer is that it is burned completely. Leviticus 6:23 gives the rule: every grain offering for a priest is burned completely, and none of it is eaten. That's different from the grain offering in Leviticus 6:14 to 16, where Aaron and his sons eat the remainder. So the priests eat from that one, but a grain offering for a priest goes up in full. Nothing left over, and no plate.

The answer is True. The priest who offers the sin offering is the one who eats it. It must be eaten in a holy place, in the courtyard of the Tent of Meeting (Leviticus 6:26). The text calls it most holy, and Leviticus 6:27 says anything that touches its flesh becomes holy. I think that tells us this meal was serious business. Me, I've scarfed down a broken cookie over the counter in about two seconds, so I'm taking notes.

The answer is that it must be broken. A clay pot used to boil the sin offering must be broken. If it's boiled in a bronze pot instead, that pot must be scoured and rinsed with water (Leviticus 6:28). Two kinds of pot, two instructions. Bronze gets a scrub and clay gets broken, so I'm glad I only deal with cookie sheets.

The answer is False. Leviticus 6:30 says, "…no sin offering may be eaten if its blood has been brought into the Tent of Meeting to make atonement in the Holy Place; it must be burned." The rule that any male among the priests may eat it has this one exception. It's a small clause, friends, but it changes everything.

The word is "sin." Leviticus 7:7 says, "The guilt offering is like the sin offering; the same law applies to both." Both are most holy, both are slaughtered where the burnt offering is slaughtered, and males among the priests may eat them in a holy place. There's one exception for the sin offering: if its blood is brought into the Tent of Meeting to make atonement in the Holy Place, it must be burned (Leviticus 6:30).

The answer is False. Meat from a peace offering eaten on the third day "…will not be accepted," says Leviticus 7:18. It also "…will not be credited to the one who presented it…" Leviticus 7:17 says anything left until the third day must be burned up.

The answer is that the person is cut off from his people. An unclean person who eats meat from the peace offering that belongs to the LORD must be cut off from his people (Leviticus 7:20). Leviticus 7:21 says the same about someone who touches something unclean and then eats the meat. This is a heavy part of the passage, friends. I think it's one to read slowly.

The answer is all the Israelites. The LORD says, "Speak to the Israelites and say, 'You are not to eat any of the fat of an ox, a sheep, or a goat'" (Leviticus 7:23). Up to now the laws were mostly for the priests. This one goes to the whole camp, like a message that lands in everyone's group chat.

The answer is Aaron and his sons. The fat goes up in smoke on the altar, and the breast goes to Aaron and his sons. The person presenting the offering brings it with his own hands and waves the breast before the LORD (Leviticus 7:30). Then Leviticus 7:34 says the LORD has given it to Aaron the priest and his sons as a permanent portion. That's a lot of arm work for a breast he doesn't get to keep. I know that feeling, I've held a whole tray of cookies at a party and been told they were for someone else.

The answer is True. "The son of Aaron who presents the blood and fat of the peace offering shall have the right thigh as a portion" (Leviticus 7:33). Leviticus 7:32 says the people give the right thigh to the priest as a contribution from their peace offering. The breast goes to Aaron and his sons, and the right thigh goes to the priest who presents the offering.

The answer is that He commanded them to present their offerings to the LORD. Leviticus 7:38 says the LORD gave these laws to Moses on Mount Sinai "…on the day He commanded the Israelites to present their offerings to the LORD in the Wilderness of Sinai." That sums up the whole stretch of laws, friends. It's good to end where the text ends.
